items.note: the facts, in reading order, one <li> each (RFC §3.1). label is the key, rendered by the library's Eyebrow (§7 Q3); value is optional inline content after it — omitted (or null) for a key alone, then no space and no value span. Product content, passed through untouched. Empty → the component renders nothing. `label`, not `key`: key is reserved by React

tone.note: the key colour for the whole strip, forwarded to every key's Eyebrow as its own tone (§7 Q4): fg/dim by default, or accent/default, which follows the accent axis. One tone per strip. No other prop — no children, size, as, separator (§7 Q6), rating (§7 Q5), className or layout prop

a11y.semanticStructure: Exactly one <ul class="ll-meta-strip" role="list"> holding one <li class="ll-meta-strip-item"> per entry of items, in order — no wrapper, nothing between two li (RFC §3.4, §4.1, §7 Q8). Each li holds the key's Eyebrow (<span class="ll-eyebrow ll-eyebrow--{tone}">) and, when a value is present, one literal space then <span class="ll-meta-strip-value">, so the DOM text reads "label value". A list, not a dl: two of the site's content shapes have no definition. No heading semantics, no live region, no accessible name on the list, no ARIA attribute beyond role="list". The uppercase of the key is the Eyebrow's CSS text-transform, so assistive tech reads the author's casing. Empty items renders nothing, never an empty list.
a11y.keyboard: Nothing to do: no interactive element, nothing focusable — no a, button, input or tabindex is rendered by the component (RFC §3.3, §4.2). Interactive content in a value is not expected; if the product passes one it keeps its own semantics and focus, product-side.
a11y.decisions: role="list" is explicit because WebKit (Safari + VoiceOver) drops list semantics from a list styled list-style: none (RFC §4.3 — the lot-1 orchestrator's decision, 2026-10-13, for the design lead's review). Contrast is computed by the contrast gate from resolved tokens over pairs already declared in contrast-pairs.json — the component adds none: the value is fg/mute on bg/default; the key, through the Eyebrow, is fg/dim on bg/default and accent/default on bg/default, scored once per accent; 11px is normal-size text (WCAG 1.4.3, 4.5:1). The dashed top rule is decoration, not an information-bearing boundary, so WCAG 1.4.11 does not apply and no line/rule pair is declared. No rating and no separator are rendered (§7 Q5, Q6), so nothing is aria-hidden. Text spacing (WCAG 1.4.12): no fixed height, no clipping, wrapping rows; the 0.06em tracking and 1.4 line-height are the type/meta tokens (§7 Q2) — a design arbitration already made, not an accessibility defect to reopen.
a11y.notes: Implemented per RFC §4; this status moves to pass only through the accessibility engine gate, never by assertion.
